Task Name: D01 — Validate Core Vulnerability Sources & Build the First Ingestion Prototype
Description:
Goal: Prove that real CVE records can be fetched, preserved and normalized into a useful draft object.

Why: Research becomes an implementable contract; prevents claiming universal coverage.

Research: What does CVE.org provide versus NVD enrichment?; Which official API, feed or download path supports this sample and later bulk sync?; What are the current authentication, quota, update and redistribution rules?; Which source owns each field, and how do affected ranges, CPE and missing fixed versions affect matching?

Inputs: Proposal requirements; One supported Linux release and Windows lab candidate

Implementation:
1. Create vulnerability-intelligence/ and a README with the sample command, Python environment, input CVE list and output locations. Keep API credentials outside the repository.
2. Choose 10–20 published representative CVEs: complete and missing-score records, amended/rejected cases where available, several product types, affected ranges and missing fixed-version information. Save the selection rationale.
3. Read the retained CVE and NVD source documentation. Record the exact official retrieval mechanism, authentication, current quota evidence, update behavior and usage/attribution conditions in research/source-comparison.md. Mark unverifiable limits as unresolved.
4. Implement collectors/cve_org.py to fetch each selected official CVE record. Preserve the untouched response plus source URL, retrieved_at, status, source revision/schema and content hash in raw/.
5. Implement collectors/nvd.py to fetch the same CVE IDs from NVD. Preserve NVD responses separately; log missing enrichment or failed requests without replacing the CVE record or advancing a false success marker.
6. Compare identifiers, descriptions, dates, scores, affected products/ranges, CPE, references and remediation fields. Document which assertions are provider-specific, missing or conflicting.
7. Draft schema/vulnerability-schema-v0.1.json with internal/external IDs, separate provider assertions, raw revision references, affected-range semantics, source timestamps and explicit missing fields. This draft is input to D02, not the final shared schema.
8. Build normalizers/sample.py to combine references to both raw records into normalized sample objects without silently choosing a winner for conflicting fields. Do not derive fixed versions from guesswork.
9. Write normalized/samples.jsonl and raw/manifest.json. Validate every selected sample against the draft schema and preserve partial cases with clear errors or missing-field flags.
10. Repeat the process from saved raw files, then ask Mahrous/Omar to run the README and review the field comparison. Save successful and failed test results before handing the prototype to D02 and D03.

Technical approach: Python collector prototype, official CVE records plus independent NVD enrichment, raw JSON and a draft schema. This is a local-file spike; D02 owns the validated shared schema, and D03 owns the production intake pipeline.

Outputs: vulnerability-intelligence/research/source-comparison.md; vulnerability-intelligence/collectors/cve_org.py; vulnerability-intelligence/collectors/nvd.py; vulnerability-intelligence/normalizers/sample.py; vulnerability-intelligence/raw/manifest.json; vulnerability-intelligence/normalized/samples.jsonl; vulnerability-intelligence/schema/vulnerability-schema-v0.1.json; vulnerability-intelligence/README.md

Testing: Fetch the same 10–20 CVEs from both sources and compare IDs, dates and field presence; Replay saved raw records through the normalizer and compare stable output; Make one source unavailable and verify an explicit partial result without invented enrichment

DONE criteria: Both collectors successfully retrieve real data for the representative sample; unavailable or incomplete cases have explicit outcomes.; 10–20 selected CVEs are exercised, with selection rationale and the same IDs compared across both sources.; Original CVE and NVD responses, retrieval metadata and hashes are preserved separately.; Source differences, authoritative/provider-specific fields, missing fields and unresolved quota/terms checks are documented.; A draft internal JSON schema exists and normalized sample records validate against it.; Replaying saved raw responses produces stable normalized records without discarding conflicts or inventing remediation.; Another team member reproduces collection/normalization from the README and records the review.

Risks: Source breadth consumes the semester.; Using a different source, observation, model or contract revision without recording it can make the handoff or reported result irreproducible.

Fallback: CVE + one Ubuntu release + KEV/EPSS first; additional vendors adapter-by-adapter.

Support handoff: Mahrous: Review applicability, policy and safety boundaries in the expected outcomes; challenge unknown and denied cases. Focus: Validate Core Vulnerability Sources & Build the First Ingestion Prototype. When: At the input/fixture review and again before D01 acceptance; coordinate after its prerequisites are available. Deliver: reviews/d01-mahrous.md — Reviewed decision outcomes and blocking policy questions
Omar: Review schemas, integration fields, API/error behavior and artifact consumption; reproduce the package handoff. Focus: Validate Core Vulnerability Sources & Build the First Ingestion Prototype. Task Name: D03 — Build Bulk CVE Ingestion and Incremental Update Processing
Description:
Goal: Load a CVE baseline, then apply new, changed and rejected records without duplicates or lost updates.

Why: Freshness is a data pipeline, not retraining an LLM every two days.

Research: Which official snapshot and revision mechanism will the selected CVE adapter use?; How will the cursor advance only after durable processing?; How will schema changes, source rejection and catch-up after downtime be represented?

Inputs: D02 schema; CVE official snapshot/repository

Implementation:
1. Create the listed output files or equivalent paths in the agreed product repository; record the package ID and prerequisite fixture revisions in the README or implementation notes.
2. Bootstrap a selected recent fixture slice then a complete chosen baseline; pin source commit/hash.
3. Fetch changes on a proposed two-hour schedule; persist last successfully processed commit/checkpoint.
4. Parse records using dataVersion; preserve CNA and ADP assertions with source labels.
5. Handle PUBLISHED and REJECTED changes; invalidate derived findings/retrieval entries without deleting history.
6. Commit checkpoint only after validated records and change events persist; on missed history use bounded reconciliation.
7. Log first_seen, normalized_at and available_to_query_at.
8. Run the package testing checklist below, save the observed results with input/revision IDs, and have Omar review the handoff before declaring completion.

Technical approach: Official CVEListV5 baseline plus incremental changes, checksums, idempotent upserts and durable checkpoints. Choose exact download mechanics from D01 evidence; no scraping dependency.

Outputs: backend/app/intelligence/cve_sync.py; backend/app/intelligence/checkpoints.py; fixtures/sync/change-sequence.jsonl; tests/intelligence/test_cve_sync.py; docs/runbooks/cve-sync.md

Testing: Import a fixed snapshot twice and assert unchanged logical counts; Replay publish, modify and reject revisions and inspect history; Crash before checkpoint commit, resume and prove no record was skipped

DONE criteria: New/amended/rejected fixtures all propagate correctly.; Crash during batch can resume with no duplicate records or skipped checkpoint.; Upstream outage makes stale status visible.; Every listed deliverable exists or has an explicitly documented equivalent path.; The testing checklist has recorded results and any unresolved failures are disclosed.; A supporting reviewer can reproduce the documented process from the named inputs without private setup assumptions.

Risks: Git history gaps or schema changes silently skip records.; Using a different source, observation, model or contract revision without recording it can make the handoff or reported result irreproducible.

Fallback: Resume from verified snapshot and reconcile IDs; quarantine unknown versions.

Support handoff: Omar: Review schemas, integration fields, API/error behavior and artifact consumption; reproduce the package handoff. 1. Create the listed output files or equivalent paths in the agreed product repository; record the package ID and prerequisite fixture revisions in the README or implementation notes.
2. Use API2/feed2, not retired legacy feeds; establish throttling using verified developer limits at implementation.
3. Process modified-time windows with overlap, deduplication and pagination; retain window checkpoint.

5. Do not require NVD CVSS or CPE before showing a CVE; display enrichment state.
6. Handle 429/backoff, larger payloads and schema additions; when history gives a GitHub link fetch current record through allowlisted adapter.

3. Document each component placement and connection: UI/TLS entry, API, worker/job ledger, PostgreSQL, evidence volumes, model/embedding endpoint and isolated runner. 4. Create a staging configuration with fixture data and a restricted demo/pilot configuration. Pin release/image versions and provide a configuration template with placeholder values only; provision runtime secrets separately.
5. Configure the selected hostname/DNS and TLS termination route after the environment gate. Compare the already-supported proxy approaches and pick one through a small test; public certificate automation and private/on-prem certificate trust have different validation and renewal requirements. Trust forwarded headers only from the configured proxy boundary.

Research: Which exact artifact/version/license and owner apply to each enabled dependency?; Are internal use, commercial service use, redistribution, derived output and attribution treated differently?; Which tools send prompts, telemetry or inventory outside the deployment boundary?; What retention, support entitlement, update and end-of-life rules must the selected customer profile satisfy?; Can data be sold or shared under the actual source rights and customer agreement?

Inputs: Scope baseline 2026-10-23.r2; Retained source register and package inputs from: current team requirements

Implementation:
1. Reuse D01 source register and existing licensing analysis; open a separate tool/model/data-rights register.
2. Inventory only enabled dependencies and exact candidate revisions; distinguish source code, weights and source content.
3. Attach official terms/license URLs, review date, attribution obligations and unresolved questions to each row.
4. Trace inventory, prompts, logs, embeddings and telemetry across the proposed trust boundary.
5. Classify each row allowed-for-this-use, restricted, unverified or excluded; an unverified commercial right is a release gate.
6. Write a business-model hypothesis around software/workflow value, not assumed resale of public feeds or customer data.
7. Review with Omar and Hams; give each affected package a required configuration or replacement action.
8. Define recurring review after dependency/terms changes and before a customer deployment.

Technical approach: Evidence-based trust/rights register with release-specific scope; legal or procurement confirmation remains required where the terms are unclear.

Outputs: governance/tool-trust-register.csv; governance/data-rights-matrix.csv; governance/data-flow-boundaries.md; business/value-and-distribution-hypotheses.md; governance/README.md

Testing: Trace one record and one assistant question through logs, indexes and external endpoints.; Check every enabled distribution artifact has a rights disposition and evidence link.; Remove an unqualified external tool and verify the disclosed local/core workflow still has a path.

DONE criteria: Each enabled source/tool/model has version, owner, rights, evidence, review date and renewal trigger.; Commercial redistribution and customer-data sharing are never assumed from public availability.; Unresolved restrictions identify an owner and block the relevant release capability.; Amr hands concrete config/license actions to Omar/Hams and the business assumptions are labelled.

Risks: Software license is mistaken for rights to all ingested content.; A cloud trace integration leaks sensitive evidence.

Fallback: Exclude the unqualified dependency or restrict the capability to an explicitly permitted internal demo; do not call it commercially cleared.

Task Name: P17 — Validate Disconnected Installation and Versioned Update Bundles
Description:
Goal: Install and operate the qualified on-prem profile without runtime internet access and prove a controlled update/restore procedure.

Why: On-prem is a required product direction. Disconnected operation needs images, models, evidence, identity and updates beyond a local LLM.

Research: Which exact CPU/GPU architecture, RAM, disk and container runtime pass the measured profile?; Which images, model/tokenizer files, embedding artifacts, packages and source snapshots must be carried offline?; What remains usable when intelligence or patch repositories cannot be refreshed?; How will the target verify bundle authenticity, schema compatibility, rollback eligibility and imported source age?; Can local/private DNS, certificate trust/renewal and identity work without runtime public internet access?

Inputs: Scope baseline 2026-10-23.r2; Retained source register and package inputs from: P14, A06, A09, D18

Implementation:
1. Freeze a profile from P14/A09 including capacity, capability flags, local identity, secrets and allowed connections.
2. Build a connected staging bundle with pinned image digests, model revisions, configuration templates, source snapshots, migrations and license notices.
3. Use image save/load for container images; separately export models, database/evidence backup and optional approved package repository content.
4. Create a manifest with artifact hashes, versions, source timestamps and compatibility rules; establish an offline-verifiable signed manifest or authenticated trusted-transfer procedure before claiming authenticity.
5. Validate the bundle and import into a clean lab host with public egress blocked; install without a first-run network download.
6. Run login, inventory import, deterministic assessment, ranked queue and local retrieval/assistant checks; declare any disabled capability explicitly.
7. Reject tampered, incompatible and unauthorized bundles; apply an allowed update transactionally with backup and tested recovery.
8. Measure install time, footprint and restore results; hand over operator instructions and enterprise qualification gaps.

Technical approach: Extend retained Compose deployment and local PostgreSQL/evidence paths; no Kubernetes requirement. Offline qualification is a planned product milestone, not a claim that the current planning website runs the product.

Outputs: deployment/offline/bundle-manifest.schema.json; deployment/offline/export-bundle.sh; deployment/offline/import-bundle.sh; deployment/offline/runbook.md; deployment/offline/qualification-report.md

Testing: Install on a clean qualified host with internet egress blocked and inspect denied connection logs.; Exercise missing model/image, wrong architecture, stale source, tampered bundle and incompatible migration cases.; Restore database and evidence together, then prove citations and assessment revisions still resolve.; Run the same reviewed assistant questions locally; a disabled assistant is a disclosed degraded profile, not a full-AI offline pass.; Repeat the enabled workflow using the documented private hostname/certificate and local identity with public egress blocked; no hidden public DNS or certificate enrollment step is allowed at runtime.

DONE criteria: Clean install uses only approved bundle artifacts with no hidden download.; All enabled core capabilities pass with public egress blocked.; Bundle authenticity/integrity and compatibility checks reject the negative cases.; Source freshness and patch-content availability are honestly displayed.; An operator reproduces installation, update and recovery from the runbook.

Risks: Runtime startup pulls a tokenizer, font, image, identity or telemetry dependency.; An image archive is mistaken for a complete application backup.; Offline feed refresh cannot meet connected freshness targets.

Fallback: Ship a qualified connected on-prem milestone first and label disconnected qualification pending; model failure degrades to cited deterministic cards, not a cloud call without permission.

Task Name: A17 — Compare Rule-Based, AI-Assisted and Hybrid Prioritization on Reviewed Organization Scenarios
Description:
Goal: Determine where AI adds measurable prioritization value over a transparent baseline without changing applicability, safety or approval authority.

Why: The existing A15 compares final contributions but does not implement a separately owned AI-ranking experiment. Hams owns the overall AI-powered prioritization capability; domain packages supply evidence and integration.

Research: Compare transparent rules, frozen-feature/classical ranking candidates, bounded LLM ranking and rules-first hybrid: required labels, compute, latency, stability and failure modes. No winner is preselected.; Can organization context change useful order while hard eligibility and policy constraints remain unchanged?; Do we have enough reviewed outcomes for learned ranking? If not, compare constrained inference-only candidates and disclose label limits.; How do missing EPSS/KEV/context, large candidate volumes, ties, duplicates and maintenance conflicts affect results?

Inputs: A02 Amr-prepared provenance/context bundle frozen by A03; D12 versioned baseline, security factors and relevance rubric; D15 independent applicability cases; D14 eligible remediation actions; A04 baseline classification outputs only where their uncertainty is recorded

Implementation:
1. Freeze the A13 ranking protocol and receive the complete A02/D12/D14/D15 input bundle; missing bundles block experiment runs, not initial literature review.
2. Research and document strongest realistic rule/AI/hybrid alternatives, label needs, cost/privacy and deployment limits before choosing the candidate.
3. Implement the shared offline harness and deterministic comparison adapters; validate input/output schema with Omar.
4. Run one low-resource AI candidate and a constrained hybrid; keep hard policy gates outside model control.
5. Evaluate per A13 with independent security review; run context/stability/failure ablations and paired time trials.
6. Publish the recommendation, negative results and reproducibility README; hand qualified outputs or baseline-retention decision to Omar.

Technical approach: RESEARCH REQUIRED: reuse D12 rules and A02/A03 data. First build a Python offline comparison harness; choose one low-resource AI candidate after evidence review, then test rules-first hybrid constrained ordering. No fine-tuning in current execution. LLM text is not an authoritative risk probability.

Outputs: research/prioritization/approach-comparison.md; experiments/prioritization/run_comparison.py; experiments/prioritization/configs/; reports/prioritization/rule-ai-hybrid-benchmark.md; reports/prioritization/recommended-approach.md; contracts/prioritization/ranking-result.schema.json; experiments/prioritization/README.md

Testing: Use identical candidate action sets, evidence revisions, allowed context and held-out cases for all methods.; Compare CVSS-only, KEV-first and D12 baseline to AI and hybrid; report cases where each loses.; Repeat stochastic candidates and change one context variable at a time; test missing inputs, injection, malformed output, excessive candidate volume and forbidden policy overrides.; Run blinded paired analyst tasks; separate correctness, review time and explanation usefulness.

DONE criteria: All three approach families are compared on the declared supported cases; unavailable learned methods have evidence-based exclusion reasons.; Every input/output and expert judgement has a recorded revision and provenance; holdout is not used for selection.; Zero observed forbidden eligibility/permission overrides in the declared test suite; this is a test result, not a universal safety guarantee.; Report quality/stability/time/latency/cost metrics, failures and uncertainty against predeclared A13 gates.; Recommend AI, hybrid or baseline based on measured evidence; retaining baseline is a valid successful experiment.; All four supporting reviewers have explicit disposition records.

Risks: Sparse or synthetic labels can make gains misleading; expert rankings can disagree.; LLM position bias, candidate truncation, randomness and confident unsupported reasoning.; Added AI latency or reviewer effort can erase ranking benefit.

Fallback: Keep D12 production order and cited explanations; show AI experiment as unqualified/offline. Do not delay core inventory, approval or verification.
